Balcony Herb Plan
Introduction
Growing herbs on a balcony is a rewarding and practical way to enhance your culinary endeavors while
enjoying the benefits of gardening in limited spaces. This guide will walk you through setting up a functional
balcony herb garden focusing on two popular herbs: basil and mint.
Basil
Practical Setup Steps
Containers: Choose pots with good drainage. Terracotta or ceramic pots with drainage holes are ideal.
Soil: Use a well-draining potting mix, ideally with added compost for rich nutrients.
Placement: Place pots in an area with plenty of sunlight, around 6-8 hours a day.
Watering and Care
Frequency: Water when the top inch of the soil feels dry. Basil prefers moderate moisture.
Maintenance: Pinch off flower spikes promptly to encourage leaf growth.
Harvesting
Begin harvesting when the plants are about 6 inches tall. Regular harvesting encourages bushiness and
growth.
Mint
Practical Setup Steps
Containers: Choose a large pot to prevent mint from spreading uncontrollably.
Soil: Use rich, well-draining soil similar to that of basil.
Placement: Mint thrives in both sun and partial shade; ensure at least part-day sun.
Watering and Care
Frequency: Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged.
Maintenance: Trim often to manage growth and prevent flowering.
Safety Note
Keep mint contained in pots to prevent it from overtaking other plants.
General Tips
Fertilizing: Use a balanced, water-soluble fertilizer every 4-6 weeks during the growing season.
Pest Management: Use neem oil or soap spray for common pests.

Conclusion
With these steps and tips, even a small balcony can become a lush, productive herb garden, providing fresh
basil and mint to enhance your cooking and drinks all season long.
